info.title: RSVP Notification API
info.description: Lane 23: authorized celebration recipients, own preferences and notification status. Legacy devices belong to lane 24; root preferences deprecated pending frontend adoption. Lane 24 registers scoped installations and exposes per-device push ticket/receipt status. Provider acceptance is not proof of physical reception. 1.3.0: guests may be reachable by phone only (E.164 from Guest becomes SMS and WHATSAPP contacts) and a host can synchronize every guest of a celebration with one bulk call, which also releases events held in WAITING_CONTEXT. 1.4.0: Notification.readAt and POST .../notifications/{notificationId}/read (host and guest, idempotent, own notifications only); per-recipient quiet hours (quietHours, source RECIPIENT or DEFAULT) and per-event-type preferences (eventTypes keyed by template, only the types of the caller's audience) on GET/PATCH preferences. Compatibility: Preferences and Notification only gain fields; PATCH {channels} keeps working; clients must tolerate new properties.

post.description: Legacy alias: celebrationId in JSON; prefer scoped /celebrations/{id}/devices.

delete.description: Legacy alias; never put a push token in a URL.

kind.description: GUEST: contacts and preferred locale are read from Guest/RSVP with the host's own credential. HOST: only the host themself.

contacts.description: Extra channel contacts (e.g. PUSH). EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP for a GUEST always come from Guest/RSVP.

put.description: Host with MANAGE access. For a GUEST the email, phone (as SMS and WHATSAPP contacts, when the deployment enables those channels) and preferred locale are read from Guest/RSVP with the host's own credential. Events that arrived before the profile existed (WAITING_CONTEXT) are released immediately.

Host with MANAGE access. One call synchronizes the whole guest list (or a subset) from Guest/RSVP using the caller's own credential, in a single transaction, then releases every event held in WAITING_CONTEXT. Idempotent. Guest/RSVP also calls this endpoint by itself after a host registers or imports guests, so the UI normally needs it only to repair or to cover guests who registered publicly.

post.description: Idempotent: the first read time is kept. Only the caller's own notification; another recipient's, another tenant's or an unknown id is 404. The body is optional (an empty JSON object is accepted).

415.description: Send application/json when a body is present

post.description: Idempotent: the first read time is kept. Only the caller's own notification; another recipient's, another tenant's or an unknown id is 404. The body is optional (an empty JSON object is accepted).

415.description: Send application/json when a body is present

locale.description: Guest locale synchronized from Guest API.

readAt.description: First time the recipient marked it read; null while unread.

guestIds.description: Optional subset. Omitted: every non-erased guest of the celebration.

skipped.description: Erased guests (never restored), kind conflicts or requested ids Guest does not know.

rejected.description: Guests whose contact data failed validation; no personal data is echoed.

QuietHours.description: Silence window in the celebration time zone, hours 0-23; start equal to end disables the silence. Notifications are deferred, never dropped.

source.description: DEFAULT is the service-wide schedule (22-08 unless configured).

EventTypePreferences.description: Template key -> enabled. Guests get giftConfirmed, giftRejected, rsvpChanged, rsvpConfirmed, rsvpDeclined; hosts get celebrationPublished, companionRequested, giftRequested, leadCapReached. Unlisted/unset types are enabled.

GuestBearer.description: Opaque Guest bearer validated with Guest API; never use in a URL.
